trial_court: Learned Judicial Magistrate, Ist Class, Baijnath, District Kangra, H.P., Cr.MMO No. 358 of 2016
case_name: Ashwani K. Lal vs Deepa Kumari Chauhan
facts_of_case: The wife was granted maintenance under Section 125 Cr.P.C. The husband filed objections to the execution of the maintenance, which were dismissed by the trial court except for December 2014. The husband appealed to this court.

legal_principles.principle: A wife is not entitled to Maintenance Allowance from her husband if she is living in adultery.
legal_principles.held: Adultery is the sexual intercourse of two persons, either of whom is married to a third person. This clearly supposes the subsistence of marriage between the husband and wife and if during the subsistence of marriage, the wife lives in adultery, she cannot claim Maintenance Allowance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

legal_principles.principle: A wife is not entitled to Maintenance Allowance from her husband if she has refused to live with him without any sufficient reason.
legal_principles.held: If the marriage subsists, the wife is under a legal and moral obligation to live with her husband and to fulfil the marital obligations. She cannot, without any sufficient reason, refuse to live with her husband.

legal_principles.principle: A wife is not entitled to Maintenance Allowance from her husband if they are living separately by mutual consent.
legal_principles.held: Under this provision, a wife is not entitled to any Maintenance Allowance from her husband if she is living in adultery or if she has refused to live with her husband without any sufficient reason or if they are living separately by mutual consent.

outcome.final_order: The wife is entitled to receive maintenance for a period of seven months.
